newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian army base had just 25 rifles - report.
newsitem.headline: Colombian army base had just 25 rifles - report.

text.p: The army base in Colombia's southwest jungle overrun by leftist guerrillas late last month had just 25 working rifles for the 150 soliders defending it, Colombian radio reported on Friday.

The Caracol radio network based its report on testimony from a kidnap victim who said he was held along with soldiers captured by rebels who overran the Las Delicias military base on Aug. 30 and freed recently after more than seven months in captivity.

According to official accounts, 37 soliders were killed and as many as 67 taken prisoner by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas who destroyed the base in southern Putumayo province in one of the single worst attacks the military has suffered in more than three decades of war.

But Caracol quoted the kidnap victim as saying only 50 soldiers were held captive since 10 had died of wounds or sickness and seven others were actually guerrillas who had infiltrated the army base disguised as soldiers.
The kidnap victim was not identified by name, but Caracol said the FARC had received a large ransom in exchange for his release.

He was quoted as saying the soliders told him Las Delicias was equipped with 200 assault rifles for the 150 soliders manning it on Aug. 30. Only 25 of the rifles were in working condition, however, facilitating the rebel assault.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, grew out of peasant militias formed in 1948. Military officials say it specialises in kidnappings and protection of rural drug operations.
